articles.title: “I had to stop”: Travis Kelce mother Donna Kelce opens up on the dream she gave up to raise him and Jason Kelce
articles.summary: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, and his brother, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon Jason Kelce, have established multiple businesses
articles.body: Travis Kelce, the Kansas City Chiefs’ tight end, and his brother, the former Philadelphia Eagles’ icon Jason Kelce, have established multiple businesses together after having successful careers on the field. Both Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce have also been public about how much their parents, Ed Kelce and Donna Kelce, have supported them through all the difficult phases in their lives. Amid the new season, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother, Donna Kelce, has reflected on how she gave up on her dreams for her children.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce reflects on the dream she had to give up for themIn an interview on Kylie Kelce’s popular podcast, Not Gonna Lie, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce said, “I did learn how to be a pilot before I had children…”Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s mother Donna Kelce added, “I actually went up and flew a plane…”Soon after learning how to fly, priorities changes for Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s parents, Ed and Donna Kelce.Donna Kelce added, “I did, but we wanted to have children, and it was really expensive, so I had to stop…Ed and I decided, well, we should probably get a house and start having kids.”To this, Jason Kelce’s wife Kylie Kelce added, "That is so cool! Does Jason know that?"Donna Kelce responded as, "I don't know if he knows it or not — I don't know if I've ever really brought it up," she said, laughing.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s parents and especially, their mother, Donna Kelce, has been a driving force behind their successful careers both on and off the field.In many of their interviews, both Travis Kelce and his older brother, Jason Kelce, have spoken about how Donna Kelce has been a strong source of strength and support to both of them.While there has been a considerable amount of buzz around Travis Kelce’s personal life, Donna Kelce has kept things private and has always respected the privacy he wants to have in his life.Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s bond could be attributed to how Donna Kelce raised them bothMany have also praised Donna Kelce for the bond that Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce share with one another.Despite playing in rival teams, both Travis Kelce and his older brother Jason Kelce have always shared a close bond with one another and have remained the best of friends with each other.After retiring from the league, Jason Kelce joined Travis Kelce on a number of ventures together as their podcast, New Heights, has been highly successful and recently, signed a $100 million deal with Amazon.For now, the focus remains on Travis Kelce as he breaks records on the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: "Tom has kept his distance from falling in love": Tom Brady reportedly avoids serious with Candice Swanepoel after Gisele Bündchen heartbreak
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel may be enjoying their new romance, but reports suggest they have different expectations about where it could lead.
articles.body: Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel may be enjoying their new romance, but reports suggest they have different expectations about where it could lead. The retired NFL quarterback, who has kept his personal life relatively private since his divorce from Gisele Bündchen, is reportedly in no rush to make things official. Swanepoel, meanwhile, appears more comfortable bringing their relationship into the public eye. Their reported differences have already sparked questions about whether the two are looking for the same kind of commitment.Tom Brady and Candice Swanepoel reportedly have different relationship expectationsBrady and Swanepoel reportedly began seeing each other in June, although news of their relationship only surfaced last weekend. Both are based in Miami, where they are said to have kept their meetings discreet for several months.However, a source cited by the Daily Mail claims the relationship may be moving at different speeds for the two stars. While Swanepoel reportedly wants something more serious, Brady appears content with keeping things casual.“Candice is definitely the one who has been more eager to get this relationship out there, while Tom is happy to enjoy what they have without putting too much of a label on it,” the source said.The insider also suggested that Brady has no plans to publicly embrace a serious relationship anytime soon.“He’s not going to broadcast it anytime soon because he enjoys being known as the bachelor,” the source continued. “His relationship mindset only makes the women he does hook up with want him more because they want to attain what might be unattainable.”At 49, Brady has attracted attention for his romantic life since ending his marriage to Bündchen in 2022. Swanepoel, 38, also has a family of her own, sharing two sons with her former fiancé, Hermann Nicoli. Brady has three children from his relationships with Bündchen and Bridget Moynahan.Tom Brady's priorities reportedly remain family and Fox broadcasting careerBrady's approach to dating may have a lot to do with how he has chosen to organise his life after his divorce. According to the insider, the seven-time Super Bowl champion has avoided serious romantic commitments while focusing on his children and professional responsibilities.“Since Gisele, Tom has kept his distance from falling in love and has instead had flings or hookups because his kids and his job are what is important to him,” the source said. “He knows relationships come and go, but family and football are forever, and he isn’t interested in heartache.”His broadcasting career with Fox Sports is also reportedly taking priority over settling down again.“His priority is his career, and the idea of settling into a committed relationship just isn’t at the top of his to-do list,” the insider said, adding that it could “change down the road.”Meanwhile, the reported romance has attracted additional attention following comments from fellow model Joan Smalls, who was previously linked to Brady and seemingly called Swanepoel a “backstabber.”Brady reportedly wants to stay away from the tension. For now, whether his relationship with Swanepoel develops into something more serious remains uncertain. Neither has publicly confirmed the reported differences in their expectations.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: George Kittle and wife Claire win hearts with emotional Iowa Children’s Hospital visit
articles.summary: George Kittle has never forgotten the people and places that shaped his journey.
articles.body: George Kittle has never forgotten the people and places that shaped his journey. Before returning to the spotlight at Iowa’s Kinnick Stadium, the San Francisco 49ers tight end chose to make a difference away from the football field. Alongside his wife, Claire, Kittle visited young patients at the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital. Their visit brought smiles to children facing difficult days and highlighted a charitable commitment that has remained close to the couple’s hearts throughout his NFL career.George Kittle and Claire bring smiles to young patients at Iowa Children’s HospitalWith the 49ers enjoying their bye week, Kittle returned to his former college town ahead of Iowa’s home game. However, his first priority was not football. He and Claire spent time with children receiving treatment at the University of Iowa Stead Family Children’s Hospital, creating special moments through conversations, laughter and simple gestures of kindness.The visit also reflected the couple’s plans to make hospital outreach a regular part of their charitable work through the Kittle Fund. Their foundation aims to support children battling illnesses, animal shelters and military veterans.Speaking about the inspiration behind their efforts on The Rich Eisen Show, Kittle explained how his connection with the hospital began during his college years.“Claire and I have done a bunch of community work my entire career going back to college. I think a big part of that started with the University of Iowa and the Iowa Children’s Hospital,” said Kittle.He also recalled how visiting young patients became an important part of his experience as an Iowa athlete.“Being athletes there, like we always got to do like community service stuff, go through the hospital and hang out with kids. And I think that just really stuck with us throughout my NFL career. And so the whole point of it is like our motto is we want to show up for those who show up for us.”George Kittle prepares for special role as Iowa honorary captainKittle’s return to Iowa also carries a special football connection. The former Hawkeye is set to serve as the team's honorary captain for its home game against Northwestern. He will join the team captains at midfield for the coin toss and spend time with the players in the locker room.His relationship with the children's hospital stretches back several years. In 2023, Kittle and Claire visited young patients, playing video games, signing autographs and spending time with their families. He also returned in 2019 alongside former Iowa teammate C.J. Beathard.Kittle has supported the hospital through fundraising efforts as well. He previously auctioned a specially designed championship belt signed by several NFL tight ends, with the proceeds benefiting young patients.For Kittle, returning to Iowa means more than celebrating his college football roots. It is also an opportunity to give back to a community that helped shape him, both as an athlete and as a person.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fuvest 2027: Candidatos relatam textos longos e prova cansativa | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidatos relataram maratona cansativa de leitura e destacaram questões sobre escala 6x1, literatura e atualidades no vestibular da USP.
articles.summary: Candidatos da Fuvest 2027 em Ribeirão Preto relatam maratona de leitura e destacam temas como escala 6x1 e cultura pop na primeira fase do vestibular da USP.
articles.body:
Estudantes que prestaram a primeira fase da Fuvest 2027 neste domingo (1º) em Ribeirão Preto (SP) relataram que a extensão dos textos e o nível de exigência na interpretação foram os pontos mais desafiadores do exame que dá acesso à Universidade de São Paulo (USP).

Apesar de a organização ter reduzido o total de perguntas de 90 para 80 questões nesta edição, a percepção dos vestibulandos foi de uma maratona de leitura que exigiu fôlego e concentração ao longo de 5 horas de prova.

"A prova em si não estava difícil, não estava complicada. Matemática era poucas questões, não requeria muitas contas, era mais lógica. O que cansa são os textos extensos e compridos", resume a estudante Maria Eloísa Zupane, de 17 anos, candidata ao curso de fisioterapia.

Em todo o estado de São Paulo e no centro de prova em Fortaleza (CE), 106,1 mil candidatos se inscreveram para o vestibular. Na região de Ribeirão Preto (SP) e Franca (SP), a prova mobilizou 9.377 inscritos em nove locais de aplicação.

Estudantes de Ribeirão Preto (SP) falaram sobre o que acharam da primeira fase da prova da Fuvest 2027. — Foto: Gabriel Luca/g1

A diminuição no número de questões não reduziu o peso da leitura, segundo os estudantes ouvidos pelo g1 na saída da prova em Ribeirão Preto.

Para a maioria dos vestibulandos, a Fuvest compensou o corte de dez questões aumentando a extensão dos enunciados e a densidade dos trechos de apoio.

O estudante Samuel Ribeiro, de 17 anos, candidato ao curso de história, enfatizou que o exame preservou a característica de ser uma prova de resistência intelectual.

"A prova da Fuvest é um pouco desafiadora. É bem difícil, tem questões bem extensas. Acredito que eles reduziram a quantidade de questões de 90 para 80, mas acabaram aumentando um pouco a dificuldade e os textos. A prova continua extensa e muito grande", avaliou Samuel.

O rigor linguístico e a complexidade na elaboração das perguntas também exigiram atenção redobrada dos vestibulandos para evitar a perda de foco.

Candidato ao curso de pedagogia, Luiz Henrique Bernardo Freire, de 27 anos, reforçou essa impressão. "Achei a prova bastante extensa e os textos bastante complicados", afirmou.

No mesmo sentido, Rafael Oliveira, de 18 anos, que prestou a prova para o curso de direito, apontou que a sofisticação do vocabulário exigiu concentração.

"Achei bem difícil, bem no nível da Fuvest mesmo. As questões são bem elaboradas, as palavras bem rebuscadas. Tem que ficar bem focado, senão você dispersa fácil", alertou.

Fuvest 2027: Pais ajudam estudante a localizar sala em local de prova na zona sul de Ribeirão Preto (SP) — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

Além do volume de leitura, os estudantes de Ribeirão Preto destacaram elementos específicos da prova que chamaram a atenção pela atualidade, interdisciplinaridade ou complexidade.

Keila Stefanie, de 19 anos, que tenta uma vaga para medicina, considerou o exame acessível e aprovou a inclusão de temas trabalhistas em pauta no país.

"Eu achei uma prova resolvível e eu gostei que eles usaram a escala 6 por 1 na prova", relatou.

A análise literária minuciosa foi outro ponto marcante lembrado pelos candidatos. Maria Eloísa mencionou uma questão desafiadora sobre a obra "Nebulosas", da escritora Narcisa Amália.

"Relacionava duas poesias dela, como 'Desengano', e era bem complexa. Perguntava sobre o contexto, a reação e o foco da autora", explicou a candidata.

A interdisciplinaridade nas questões de idiomas também surpreendeu os estudantes. Luiz Henrique ressaltou a profundidade cobrada no segmento de língua estrangeira.

"Achei interessante que no eixo de inglês as questões estavam envolvendo física e tudo mais, uma interpretação mais profunda do que eu esperava", contou.

Fuvest 2027: Estudantes lotam local de prova na zona sul de Ribeirão Preto (SP) na primeira fase da prova — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

A primeira fase da Fuvest 2027 contou com 80 perguntas de múltipla escolha sobre o conteúdo geral do ensino médio. A edição destacou-se por integrar a cultura pop a análises acadêmicas e sociais.

Entre as referências culturais citadas na prova, os candidatos encontraram questões sobre a displasia cleidocraniana a partir do ator Gaten Matarazzo, da série Stranger Things; o show de Bad Bunny no Super Bowl para abordar geopolítica e simbologia; a música "Meninos e Meninas", da banda Legião Urbana; e uma imagem gerada por inteligência artificial simulando um encontro entre Elis Regina e Maria Rita.

Bad Bunny segura a bandeira de Porto Rico no Super Bowl — Foto: Getty Images/via BBC

O exame abordou ainda a proposta de fim da jornada de trabalho 6x1 associada à teoria de exploração em Karl Marx, o papel de influenciadores fitness na imagem corporal, impactos das mudanças climáticas na flora e princípios da física aplicados a manobras de skate.

A Fuvest oferece nesta edição 8.147 vagas em cursos de graduação da USP. Das oportunidades disponíveis, 4.888 destinam-se à ampla concorrência, 2.053 a alunos oriundos de escolas públicas e 1.206 a estudantes de escolas públicas autodeclarados pretos, pardos ou indígenas.

Os candidatos aprovados nesta etapa farão a segunda fase nos dias 6 e 7 de dezembro. O primeiro dia abordará a prova de português e a redação, e o segundo dia trará perguntas específicas ligadas à carreira escolhida.

A divulgação dos convocados e dos locais de exame ocorre em 23 de novembro. A primeira chamada oficial para matrícula será publicada em 26 de janeiro de 2027.

articles.title: From children's hospitals to community causes: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld's millions in charity-linked support
articles.summary: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld have plenty to celebrate in their personal lives, but their charitable work offers another reason they continue to attract
articles.body: Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld have plenty to celebrate in their personal lives, but their charitable work offers another reason they continue to attract attention. The Buffalo Bills quarterback has built a strong connection with children's healthcare in Western New York, turning personal loss into a long-running effort to help families. Steinfeld, meanwhile, has used her celebrity platform to support children's hospitals and several charitable causes. Their contributions tell two different stories, but both highlight how public figures can use their influence to make a difference beyond their careers.Josh Allen's $17,000 donation started a much bigger charitable movementOne of Allen's most meaningful charitable contributions came in November 2020, following the death of his grandmother, Patricia Allen. Bills supporters began donating to John R. Oishei Children's Hospital in her memory, with many choosing $17 contributions to honour the quarterback's jersey number.The response quickly gathered momentum. When the donations approached $500,000, Allen personally pledged another $17,000 to help push the total higher. More than 23,000 contributions had already reached the hospital.The donations eventually led to the creation of the Patricia Allen Fund in December 2020. According to the hospital foundation, the fund was established with input from Allen and his family to support children receiving critical care.This became one of the most important parts of his charitable work. Instead of making a single contribution and moving on, Allen continued supporting the hospital through different campaigns and fundraising efforts.Josh Allen's other donations include a $100,000 pledge with NikeAllen had already been supporting children's healthcare before his grandmother's passing.In 2019, he committed to donating $200 to Oishei Children's Hospital for every touchdown he scored or threw. His contribution reached $10,000 by the end of the season. He also designed a limited-edition New Era cap with hospital patients and staff, with part of the sales proceeds benefiting the hospital.His involvement continued through the NFL's My Cause My Cleats campaign. Allen worked with two young patients, Charlie and Clayton, to create custom footwear. He later put the cleats up for auction, directing the proceeds towards Oishei Children's Hospital.In December 2021, Allen and Nike announced a joint $100,000 pledge to the hospital. The contribution supported patient treatment and reflected his desire to give back to the community that welcomed him after he entered the NFL.Another notable contribution came in May 2024. Allen agreed to donate $117,000 to Oishei Children's Hospital through the 117 Holes for Children's fundraising event. The money supported the Patricia Allen Fund, and he encouraged fans to match his contribution.The event eventually raised $775,000, including Allen's personal pledge.Josh Allen's $2 million charity milestone involved West Herr and New EraAllen's charitable influence has also helped bring major corporate contributions to Buffalo.In October 2022, West Herr Auto Group donated $2,000,017 to the Patricia Allen Fund. Allen attended the announcement at Oishei Children's Hospital, but the contribution came from the automotive company, not his personal finances.The additional $17 honoured his jersey number and the campaign's connection to his grandmother.His partnership with New Era has also produced impressive results. The Billustration campaign invited young patients at Golisano Children's Hospital to design special caps that Allen wore before Bills home games.The first campaign raised $140,230 through nine cap auctions in 2025. In May 2026, New Era and Allen celebrated the success by releasing a special edition cap featuring the children's designs. Every purchase benefited the Patricia Allen Fund.The initiative returned for 2026 with eight new designs created by young patients. It gave children a creative opportunity while directing more support towards families receiving hospital care.Other contributions included EA Sports' $10,000 donation to the Patricia Allen Fund in 2023, announced when Allen appeared on the Madden NFL 24 cover.These figures should not all be counted as Allen's personal donations. They demonstrate how his involvement has encouraged businesses, fans and partners to contribute.Hailee Steinfeld's charitable work includes a children's hospital campaignSteinfeld's public charitable record is less focused on large personal cash donations, but she has participated in several initiatives.One of her best-documented campaigns dates back to July 2017, when she partnered with MISSION to launch the What's Your Mission? T-shirt initiative.The campaign supported Children's Hospital Los Angeles, with $5 from every T-shirt purchase going towards the hospital.The actress and singer also spoke about her connection with the organisation and her interest in helping children and families who need medical support.Her charitable affiliations extend beyond that campaign. Public charity profiles have associated her with organisations including St. Jude Children's Research Hospital, UNICEF, the American Cancer Society, the Leukemia & Lymphoma Society, Project Sunshine, Ronald McDonald House Charities, Stand Up To Cancer and the Children's Defense Fund.However, these affiliations should not be mistaken for confirmed personal cash donations to every organisation.There has also been a report claiming that Steinfeld donated $100,000 to Ella Thompson, a young Buffalo Bills fan reportedly battling stage 4 neuroblastoma, in October 2025. However, an independently verifiable fundraising record or reliable confirmation of the contribution remains unavailable. The amount should therefore be treated as an unverified report rather than an established donation.Josh Allen and Hailee Steinfeld's generosity extends beyond financial contributionsThe couple's generosity has also appeared in smaller personal gestures.In December 2025, Allen and Steinfeld reportedly gave Buffalo Bills offensive linemen a quarter of a cow each as a Christmas present. Allen also included an infrared steak searer to help his teammates prepare the meat.The gifts were shared publicly by the wife of offensive tackle Alec Anderson. While this was not a charitable donation, it offered a glimpse into the couple's thoughtful approach to personal relationships.Their public records show different approaches to giving. Allen has developed a long-term relationship with children's healthcare organisations, particularly through the Patricia Allen Fund. Steinfeld has supported charitable campaigns and used her platform to bring attention to causes affecting children and families.There is no independently confirmed combined donation total for the couple. Still, Allen's ongoing hospital work and Steinfeld's charitable partnerships show that their influence reaches beyond football, music and Hollywood.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tom Brady drops another 'oh s***' live on Fox during appearance on 'Fox NFL Sunday'
articles.summary: Tom Brady is now a repeat offender when it comes to using foul language on live TV.
articles.body:
Legendary NFL quarterback Tom Brady is still getting a hang of this broadcasting thing. While Brady has worked hard to improve as a broadcaster over the years, there's still one area in which he could clean up: his foul language.

For the second time this season, Brady dropped an "oh s***" while live on Fox. This time around, his NSFW moment occurred during an appearance on "Fox NFL Sunday," where he was pulled into a trivia segment with Drew Brees.

The segment focused on Brady and Brees trying to name the quarterback who ranked third all-time behind them in significant stat categories. Upon giving an incorrect answer, Brady uttered "oh s***" before quickly realizing his mistake.

The desk very clearly heard Brady's mistake and saw his reaction. After a few members at the desk laughed, host Curt Menefee eventually said, "We let you get away with one, by the way. We heard you. That's OK."

Menefee then ended the segment, but both he and Michael Strahan still got in one more reference to Brady's slip-up. After Strahan mentioned the program was live, Menefee said, "[Brady's] learning."

The former quarterback may need to do a better job drilling that particular rule into his head. Sunday marked the second time this season in which Brady was caught using that expletive on the air.

His first use of that phrase came back in Week 2, when Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow. Upon seeing a replay of the play , Brady — who was in the booth calling the game — uttered "oh s***" after he saw Daniels' elbow bend the wrong way.

Brady quickly apologized for that incident, saying he "was not expecting to see that."

Following his Week 8 gaffe, Brady will call the Detroit Lions vs. Minnesota Vikings game, where he'll look to practice some language discipline after his early mistake.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Ravens QB to Undergo Surgery After Exiting on 1st Play in Return
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will undergo surgery on this thumb and will be placed on injured reserve, head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after his team's loss to the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will undergo surgery on this thumb and will be placed on injured reserve, head coach Jesse Minter told reporters after his team's loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Jackson suffered the injury to his throwing hand during his first offensive snap of Sunday's game and was later ruled out .

When he returned to the sideline, he was wearing a brace on his thumb:

Evan Washburn of CBS Sports provided an update after the initial injury, including a close-up look at the injured thumb:

To make matters worse for the Ravens, backup Tyler Huntley suffered a turf toe injury during the game and will undergo an MRI:

Huntley only played a few plays before he was replaced by emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano

Running back Justice Hill was set to be the next man up for the Ravens at quarterback if Fagnano suffered an injury, according to the CBS broadcast.

For the season, the two-time NFL MVP has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six touchdowns and one interception. He's also rushed for 144 yards and one more score.

Jackson has missed his team's last three full games (Weeks 5-7 against the Atlanta Falcons, Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals) due to a left high ankle sprain suffered against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4 .

There was hope Jackson could play against Cincinnati. He was listed as questionable and provided an encouraging report on Oct. 22, two days before the game.

"Right now, I'm headed in the right direction," Jackson told reporters after Friday's practice. "I can't call it right now, still got a grace period, so we'll see, man, hopefully. But I feel like I'm heading in the right direction right now."

Jackson was ultimately ruled out, but his return appeared imminent.

The latest injury puts the Ravens in a difficult position after falling to 4-4 on the season.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson ruled out of Bills-Ravens game with thumb injury sustained on Baltimore's first offensive play
articles.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with an apparent injury on Buffalo's first offensive play.
articles.body:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with a right thumb injury sustained on Baltimore's first offensive play from scrimmage.

The Ravens quickly ruled him out for the rest of the game.

Jackson took contact on his hand after a pass and was in immediate pain. He left the field and walked straight to the locker room. Backup Tyler Huntley took his place at quarterback.

The Ravens initially announced that Jackson was questionable to return with a thumb injury before ruling him out before the conclusion of the first quarter. The injury is to the thumb on his throwing hand.

Jackson, a two-time NFL MVP, was playing in his first game since sustaining a high-ankle sprain in Week 4 that caused him to miss three games. He returned to the 4-3 Ravens in time for the critical AFC showdown against Josh Allen and the Bills, but now he's out against the Bills and potentially for longer.

The injury is another difficult blow for Jackson and a Ravens team seeking to compete for a Super Bowl championship. Jackson is one of the game's best players when healthy, but injuries have derailed his last two seasons.

Jackson missed four games last season and was limited in several others with leg and back injuries. The Ravens were projected last season as a Super Bowl contender but finished 8-9 and missed the playoffs.

The Ravens again were projected to compete for a Super Bowl this season, but Jackson is now potentially looking at a long-term absence. Jackson, 29, is playing on the fourth year of a five-year, $260 million contract.

Team owner Steve Bisciotti has expressed his desire to make Jackson a Raven for life, but the two sides reportedly haven't engaged in substantial contract negotiations .

articles.title: “Is This Kid a Joke”: Ex-Jets HC Blasts Ashton Jeanty on Live TV After Raiders RB’s Dig at New York
articles.summary: Former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan lost his cool on live television in the build-up to Week 8. Ryan went on a rant during ESPN’s Sunday NFL Countdown a...
articles.body:
Former New York Jets head coach Rex Ryan lost his cool on live television in the build-up to Week 8. Ryan went on a rant during ESPN's Sunday NFL Countdown after Las Vegas Raiders 2nd-year running back Ashton Jeanty said that a few New York defenders don't want to make tackles.

The incident happened on Wednesday as the 3-4 Raiders were set to face the 2-5 Jets at MetLife Stadium. Jeanty, who had a poor 15-yard performance on 8 carries against the Rams, told reporters about the Jets' defense, "I think we can definitely get the run game going. Get back on track and really get after these guys. A couple guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."

This comment got to Rex Ryan, who defended his team's linebacker Demario Davis on ESPN.

"You know who hand-picked this guy when he came out of college? You're looking at him. Why? Because he knocked your face in! Is this kid a joke or what? Does he not look at the tape? Because when I see the tape, I see that. I see Demario Davis not losing a step, still playing at the top of his game. But you know what else I see? How about Mr. Tiptoe Through the Tulips, avoiding contact. This guy is soft as Charmin. Look at him. Oh, hired killer right there," Rex Ryan said on ESPN's Coach's Clicker.

Davis was drafted in the third round of the 2012 NFL Draft by the Jets. At that time, Ryan was the head coach of the franchise and a major driving force for Davis' selection. Ryan famously compared him to Hall of Famer Ray Lewis.

So, as Ryan stood next to Tedy Bruschi at the touchscreen, Ryan discussed the footage. Whilst showing Demario Davis making big hits, Ryan pointed out how Jeanty was leaning away from the contact to avoid tackles. He made his point clear that Jeanty had no right to question how physical Gang Green are.

"Look, I'm gonna tell you something, Bru. I'm gonna talk to this kid before the game. I'm going right up to him. You know me, I tell the truth. I'm going right up to him, and I say, 'Listen young man, I heard what you said. And I want you to know something, all right? We are not going to try to take you out of the game…Why? Because you are horrible. You're about the worst draft pick in the last 20 years, I think, as a running back. You stink. You're averaging 3.1 yards a carry. And guess what? Today you get your a– kicked, and you know who else does? Your teammates. It's on you, my friend.'"

When asked by Bruschi if he would go right up to him, Ryan said, "Right up to his a–." Ryan said that Jeanty's poor running was holding Las Vegas back in their four-game losing streak and his comments would weigh heavily on him Sunday.

articles.title: Seahawks announce 3 captains for NFL Week 8 vs Chicago Bears
articles.summary: Here are Seattle's captains for their prime time showdown with Chicago.

articles.title: Colts' early-round draft pick makes first start v. Jaguars
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts' rookie linebacker CJ Allen is making his first NFL start against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts' rookie linebacker CJ Allen is making his first NFL start against the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 8.

Earlier in the week, defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo strongly hinted that this would be the case. Allen did not play last week against Minnesota due to injury, but Anarumo said if he had been available, he would have started in that game as well.

Anarumo added that Allen will be the middle linebacker, although Akeem Davis-Gaither will continue to wear the green dot as the defensive signal caller.

Allen was a second-round pick by the Colts this past April, and the expectation early on was that he would start right away and wear the green dot. However, after missing time during training camp, that never came to fruition.

Instead, Allen's role as a rookie had been relatively small. While the Colts rotated heavily at the WILL linebacker position, Allen was specifically a MIKE, a role filled by Davis-Gaither, who Anarumo did not want to take off the field.

So through seven games, Allen had played only 48 defensive snaps, which includes not seeing the field at all in two contests, even though he was healthy.

articles.title: Steelers respond to 'dirty' comments from Browns' Jared Verse with in-game scrap
articles.summary: The Browns defensive end was slammed to the ground by the Steelers' left guard in the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium.
articles.body:
Cam Heyward's promise that the Steelers would "address" trash talk by Cleveland Browns defensive end Jared Verse came true during their pivotal NFL Week 8 meeting Nov. 1 at Acrisure Stadium.

Left guard Mason McCormick slammed Verse to the ground on an extra point attempt following Rico Dowdle's touchdown that put Pittsburgh up 7-0 in the first quarter.

McCormick was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play. Verse was not penalized but was seen celebrating as he and his Cleveland teammates ran off the field after the play.

The penalty ended up not hurting the Steelers, as Cleveland was forced to punt on the subsequent drive.

"They were talking crazy," Verse told reporters in his post-game news conference after the teams' Week 4 meeting in early October. "I was telling them, 'Y'all double-teaming and sliding and you're garbage.' I don't have respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra [stuff] after the game. I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a great time when I see them again."

That apparently did not sit well with the Steelers, especially considering they dropped a 27-24 decision in overtime during their trip to Cleveland on Oct. 2

Heyward said as much in an appearance on the Rich Eisen Show on Oct. 29 in anticipation of the rematch that will decide control of the AFC North division.

"Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game?" Heyward said Tuesday on The Rich Eisen show. "Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don't whine about it, baby. It's part of the game. And so, I'm looking forward to this game. It's gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say.

Who are the scariest players in NFL history? These are our choices.

"The AFC North is on fire and I'm glad I'm in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those are words that were said and they will be addressed."

The Steelers and Browns are fighting for first place in the division. The winning team will take the lead at 6-2. Cincinnati enters the week a half game behind both teams at 4-2.

The Jets moved back into the lead on a second quarter touchdown, but their edge over the Raiders did not last long.

articles.title: Gardner Minshew, Cardinals Upset Cowboys with Epic Comeback After Jacoby Brissett Benched
articles.summary: It has been a season to forget so far for the Arizona Cardinals, and they made a quarterback change Sunday during the second half of Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys with the hope of sparking some momentum.
articles.body:
It has been a season to forget so far for the Arizona Cardinals, and they made a quarterback change Sunday during the second half of Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys with the hope of sparking some momentum.

Arizona benched Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew after falling behind 17-3. Brissett was terrible throughout the game prior to his benching:

The starter went 10-of-23 for 119 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception as the Cardinals fell behind by multiple scores.

And then all Minshew did was rally the visitors to a dramatic 33-30 overtime victory.

Notably, Arizona scored a touchdown on Minshew's drive, although it wasn't because of the quarterback. He did make a seven-yard completion on his first throw before Tyler Allgeier broke loose for a 63-yard touchdown run.

That was just a sign of what was to come, as Minshew found Allgeier and Trey McBride for touchdowns in the fourth quarter to pull within three. From there, the Cowboys added a field goal and gave Minshew an opportunity to win it in crunch time trailing by six.

It appeared as if he did when he found Michael Wilson for a touchdown with six seconds remaining, although Chad Ryland missed the extra point that would have won it.

Ryland earned redemption, though, as he connected on the game-winning field goal in overtime after the two defenses traded stops.

Minshew finished 17-of-23 for 188 yards, three touchdowns and zero interceptions and likely earned himself more playing time moving forward.

Brissett is signed through just this season, so it's not as if the Cardinals are relying on him to be their franchise quarterback for the foreseeable future.

Of course, Minshew is also signed through just this season and is 30 years old. He isn't someone the Cardinals are going to be turning to for seasons to come either, meaning this benching was more about the immediate future than anything else even if he did play the role of hero.

Perhaps they will eventually give Carson Beck a chance if and when the season continues to slip further away following a 3-5 start.

Arizona selected the rookie with a third-round pick in the 2026 NFL draft after he helped lead Miami to the College Football Playoff national championship game. At some point, the NFC West team will likely want to see what it has in the rookie and could respond accordingly after benching Brissett.

For now, though, it appears as if Minshew is going to get an opportunity for a Cardinals team looking for some type of spark.

articles.title: Jack Campbell Hospitalized After Being Carted Off with Scary Injury for Lions vs. Vikings
articles.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered what appears to be a serious injury during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell suffered what appears to be a serious injury during Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings.

After making a tackle, Campbell was unable to get up on his own power and received attention from medical staff on the field before being carted off.

He was transported to a local hospital, the team announced .

Head coach Dan Campbell provided a limited update after the game:

Jack Campbell is one of the most important pieces of the Lions' defense, coming into Sunday's game leading the team in total tackles (54). He added three more tackles against the Vikings on Sunday before suffering his neck injury.

He's coming off a season in which he earned a First-team All-Pro nod after collecting a career-high 176 tackles, five sacks and three forced fumbles.

Detroit rewarded Campbell for his career season by giving him a four-year, $81 million contract extension over the offseason.

The Lions selected Campbell with the 18th overall pick in 2023 after his standout career at Iowa. The 26-year-old has since developed not only into one of the best linebackers in the league, but also into the leader of Detroit's defense.

"This is Jack Campbell's defense, and I don't hesitate when I say that," defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard said of Campbell earlier this year. "This is Jack Campbell's defense and everyone in that locker room knows it. Point blank period. It all goes through Jack."

Needless to say, losing Campbell would be a significant blow to the Lions, who are 4-2 and looking to return to the playoffs after missing the playoffs last season.

articles.title: Baker Mayfield, Bucs Beat Falcons Despite Unreal Stat That Hasn't Happened in 52 Years
articles.summary: In the modern NFL, the passing game reigns supreme. But not for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.
articles.body:
In the modern NFL, the passing game reigns supreme. But not for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday.

In a torrential downpour, the Bucs defeated the Atlanta Falcons 16-0 despite not completing a single pass. Going an entire game without a single completion is one of the rarest feats in the sport:

Steelers 1st in AFC North After Beating Browns

The Bucs and quarterback Baker Mayfield attempted just three passes during the game, relying both on a run game that recorded a team-record 324 yards on 56 attempts and a stifling defense that intercepted Michael Penix Jr. four times.

Running back Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards and a score, while Kenneth Gainwell managed 140 yards on the ground.

It was very much an "if it ain't broke, don't fix it" philosophy on offense once it was clear that the run game was working and the defense was balling. The Bucs and Falcons now have identical 3-5 records.

articles.title: Lions rally late to knock off Kyler Murray and the Vikings, the NFL's last undefeated team
articles.summary: The Lions flew ahead in the second half to beat the Vikings 19-15 at home on Sunday afternoon, even after losing linebacker Jack Campbell to a scary neck inj...
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings' undefeated run has come to an end.

Jared Goff and the Detroit Lions rallied late after losing star linebacker Jack Campbell to a scary neck injury to knock off the NFL's last undefeated team on Sunday afternoon at Ford Field. They picked up a 19-15 win over the Vikings, ending Minnesota's six-game win streak to open the 2026 campaign.

Despite their perfect record, the Vikings have struggled in recent weeks — especially offensively. They only snuck past the Indianapolis Colts last week late to maintain their undefeated streak . And for much of Sunday's contest, those struggles continued.

The Vikings entered halftime up by just a single point after what was a slow start from Kyler Murray. He went just 7 of 15 for 86 yards in the opening half, and threw a pretty bad interception while trying to force a throw just before the break. That set up a late Lions field goal.

Now, Detroit wasn't much better. Quarterback Jared Goff threw his first interception of the season in the first half, and they missed a field goal on their opening drive of the third quarter. Finally, though, Jahmyr Gibbs broke open a 30-yard run late in the third period to give the Lions their first lead of the afternoon.

To Murray's credit, he had his moments. He found Justin Jefferson for a 1-yard touchdown in the second quarter to get them on the board, and then he set up a touchdown pass to TJ Hockenson and a 2-point conversion with a wild 51-yard pass to Jordan Addison.

That didn't hold. Goff, after a few big gains from Gibbs, found a wide open Jameson Williams for a touchdown to put them in front by four with just 4:35 left. The Minnesota defense, which has been solid all season, had no answers on that drive.

The Vikings went three-and-out after that, and Murray again tried to force a ball deep to Addison on third down. They opted to punt, and the Lions simply rode out the four-point win.

Goff went 18 of 25 for 176 yards with a touchdown and an interception in the win for the Lions, which pushed them to 5-2 on the season. They've won three straight now, too. Gibbs had 153 yards and a touchdown on 23 carries, which marked his third game this season with at least 150 yards on the ground. Williams finished with 70 yards and a score on four catches.

Campbell went down early in the fourth quarter while trying to make a tackle, and had to be loaded onto a stretcher and taken off the field. Several Lions players were extremely emotional, and defensive captain Aidan Hutchinson appeared to be crying. Campbell was transported to a local hospital with a neck injury.

Murray finished 17 of 29 for 210 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the loss for Minnesota. He was the team's leading rusher with 35 yards on four carries. Addison ended with 66 yards on three catches.

While they've now lost, the Vikings are still in great position in the NFC North race. They've only won the division once in the past nine seasons, most recently in 2022. Now, they'll have to bounce back against Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills next week, which won't be an easy task. And their offensive inconsistency is still an issue they need to address if they are going to claim a division title and live up to their hot start.

How Murray and the Vikings bounce back over the next week will be key to how things go down the stretch.

articles.title: Ashton Jeanty Snaps Cut, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Cousins, Bowers, Top Raiders-Jets Players
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders edged the New York Jets, 38-33, but the backfield spotlight shifted as Ashton Jeanty saw just two carries while Mike Washington Jr. led the way with 25 carries as the Raiders' top running back.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders edged the New York Jets, 38-33, but the backfield spotlight shifted as Ashton Jeanty saw just two carries while Mike Washington Jr. led the way with 25 carries as the Raiders' top running back.

Geno Smith and the Jets had one last chance to rally, down by five, but Jeremy Chinn's game-sealing interception put the finishing touches on Las Vegas' road win.

The Jets entered Sunday's home matchup as 1.5-point favorites over the Raiders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

The Raiders improved to 4-4 behind three touchdown passes from Kirk Cousins, earning a road win as the Jets fell to 2-6.

There was plenty of scoring in the first quarter, as the Jets notched two field goals while the Raiders found the end zone in between. Cousins connected with Brock Bowers for a touchdown to give Las Vegas a 7-6 lead.

The Jets took control before halftime, scoring 17 points in the second quarter while finding the end zone on consecutive possessions. Smith connected with Isaiah Williams for an 18-yard touchdown before Adonai Mitchell hauled in a 12-yard scoring pass.

The Raiders' only score of the quarter came on a 95-yard kickoff return by Dylan Laube, as they trailed 23-14 at halftime.

The scoring continued after halftime, as Bowers hauled in his second touchdown catch of the day and Cousins added a rushing touchdown.

The Raiders were unable to take the lead into the fourth quarter, as New York's Braelon Allen rushed for a 21-yard touchdown.

A touchdown pass from Cousins to Jalen Nailor to open the fourth quarter gave the Raiders back the lead, 35-30. The Jets' Jason Sanders responded with a 31-yard field goal to cut the deficit to two points with 4:31 remaining.

The Raiders' Matt Gay added a 53-yard field goal with 27 seconds left, forcing the Jets to score a touchdown to win the game.

After the Jets drove to Las Vegas' 35-yard line, Smith threw an interception that Raiders safety Jeremy Chinn hauled in to seal the Raiders' road win.

The Raiders will hit the road to face the San Francisco 49ers at 4:25 p.m. ET, while the Jets will travel to take on the Kansas City Chiefs at 1 p.m. ET on the same day.

articles.title: Vikings Lose to Lions for 1st Loss, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Kyler, Goff, Top Players
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings fell to the Detroit Lions by the final score of 19-15 at Ford Field on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings fell to the Detroit Lions by the final score of 19-15 at Ford Field on Sunday.

With the defeat, Minnesota suffered its first loss of the season.

Steelers 1st in AFC North After Beating Browns

Detroit emerged victorious after entering the game as 3.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Here's a look at how notable fantasy players including Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and Lions passer Jared Goff fared during the contest:

The Vikings opened the game by driving down to the Lions' 38-yard line, although a 57-yard field goal attempt was unsuccessful.

Both teams traded punts on the next two possessions of the contest before Detroit was able to get on the board first, as Jake Bates connected on a 25-yard field goal.

Minnesota immediately responded with a seven-play, 74-yard drive that ended with an incredible touchdown reception by Justin Jefferson.

Neither squad was able to find much success offensively for the remainder of the second half, as the next six combined drives following Jefferson's touchdown grab resulted in four total punts and two interceptions.

The Lions eventually gained some momentum heading into halftime, as Bates nailed a 37-yard field goal just before the second quarter came to a close.

Bates missed a 46-yard field goal attempt on Detroit's first possession of the third quarter, but the Lions' defense was able to force a Vikings punt immediately afterwards.

On Detroit's next drive, Jahmyr Gibbs ran 30 yards into the end zone to give his squad a 12-7 lead.

The back-and-forth affair continued early in the fourth quarter, as T.J. Hockenson reeled in an eight-yard touchdown catch to put Minnesota back in front.

The Vikings' lead was short-lived, as Detroit quickly drove down the field before Goff connected with Jameson Williams for a seven-yard score.

Minnesota wasn't able to move the sticks on its next possession and punted the ball away with three minutes left in the fourth quarter.

The Vikings' defense couldn't hold Detroit, as the Lions picked up three first downs on their final drive to run out the clock and seal the win.

Detroit improved to 5-2, while Minnesota fell to 6-1.

articles.title: Steelers Beat Browns, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Aaron Rodgers, Deshaun Watson, Shedeur, More

Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers cruised to a victory over Deshaun Watson and the Cleveland Browns on Sunday, 27-6.

The Steelers covered the spread, entering the matchup as 3.5-point favorites over the Browns at home, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Shedeur Sanders briefly stepped in during the first quarter after Watson was sidelined with an injury, completing both of his pass attempts for two yards.

articles.title: Bills Beat Ravens, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Josh Allen, Lamar, Henry, Cook, Top Players
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills picked up a dominant double-digit win over the Baltimore Ravens at home on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills picked up a dominant double-digit win over the Baltimore Ravens at home on Sunday.

Buffalo took advantage of Lamar Jackson's early exit due to a thumb injury and ran away with a 36-10 victory. Jackson was injured on the Ravens' first play from scrimmage.

The Ravens ended up using third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano for most of the game after injuries to both Jackson and Tyler Huntley.

The complexion of the game changed early when Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury that ruled him out of the game.

The Ravens scored a single touchdown on a Derrick Henry run in the first quarter and managed to earn just 145 total yards with Tyler Huntley and then Joe Fagnano in at quarterback.

Buffalo took the lead early on a Josh Allen touchdown run and didn't turn back after that point.

Tyler Bass kicked a trio of field goals in the first and second quarters from 56, 22 and 51 yards out to open up the lead to nine points by halftime.

Allen aired the ball out in the second half to further open up the Bills' advantage.

D.J. Moore and Dalton Kincaid hauled in touchdown passes from 11 and 23 yards out to finish off the victory in the fourth quarter.

Allen became the Bills' all-time leader in passing touchdowns on the scoring throw to Kincaid.

Allen produced over 300 total yards in the victory that was easy for the Bills to earn after Jackson left the game with his injury.

Buffalo is now 5-1 and in a good spot to contend for the top seed in the AFC. The Bills face the Minnesota Vikings next Monday in a potential Super Bowl preview.

Meanwhile, the Ravens have to figure out what their quarterback situation will look like with all the injuries. The 4-4 Ravens host the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday night.

articles.title: Buccaneers register zero passing yards in rainy 16-0 win over Falcons with Baker Mayfield not throwing a single completion
articles.summary: Tampa Bay was the first team to win with no passing yards since the Buffalo Bills did so in 1974, the second such game during the Super Bowl era.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Atlanta Falcons struggled through a literal slog amid heavy rain at Raymond James Stadium for their Week 8 matchup. The Bucs trudged their way to a 16-0 win despite getting no passing yards as quarterback Baker Mayfield threw three incomplete passes.

Tampa Bay technically finished with -2 passing yards as Mayfield was sacked for a 2-yard loss by the Falcons' Harold Perkins Jr. in the third quarter. However, the Bucs generated 321 yards of offense, all of it coming on the ground. Very muddy, soggy ground at that.

Bucky Irving rushed for 170 yards on 27 carries and scored the game's lone touchdown. Kenny Gainwell added another 140 yards rushing on 25 attempts. And Mayfield ran for 14 yards in the only offense he produced on Sunday.

The Buccaneers' win without any passing yards was only the second such game in the NFL during the Super Bowl era.

The Buffalo Bills defeated the New York Jets, 16-12 , on Sept. 29, 1974 will Bills QB Joe Ferguson going 0-for-2 on passing. (Like Mayfield, he also rushed for 14 yards.) Jets Hall of Famer Joe Namath threw for 33 yards, completing 2 of 18 passes.

Fast-forwarding to 52 years later, Tampa Bay led 9-0 at halftime. But that score didn't convey just how miserable the game was to that point.

In one of the more curious halftime box scores ever seen, Mayfield had zero yards passing in the first two quarters with his two throws going incomplete. Yet the Buccaneers got three field goals from Chase McLaughlin to take the lead.

Tampa Bay did get offense from its running game with Irving rushing for 107 yards on 19 carries. The Bucs had 146 total yards at the half, all on the ground, with Gainwell contributing 27 yards and Mayfield rushing for 12.

Atlanta had 97 total yards at halftime, 67 of them on the ground from Bijan Robinson. But QB Michael Penix Jr. threw for 24 yards and three interceptions, completing 2 of 10 passes. His 24 yards were the only passing yards recorded after two quarters of play.

Penix finished 124 yards passing, but threw 4 interceptions while completing 8 of 24 throws. Jahan Dotson caught two of those passes for 95 yards, while Robinson ended up with 76 yards rushing on 19 carries.

For the Bucs, Sunday's win was their first at home this season and improved their record to 3-5. The Falcons are also 3-5 after the defeat and have lost three of their past four games. Both teams are tied for second in the NFC South, a half-game behind the first-place Carolina Panthers.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson needs surgery, headed to injured reserve with thumb injury sustained in loss to Bills
articles.summary: Jackson's headed to injured reserve with a significant injury to his thumb.
articles.body:
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson left Sunday's game against the Buffalo Bills with a right thumb sustained on Baltimore's first offensive play.

He'll need surgery to repair the injury on his throwing hand and will require a stint on injured reserve that will sideline him for four weeks weeks at a minimum. Head coach Jesse Minter announced the update after Baltimore's 36-10 loss to the Bills .

The Ravens didn't announce the precise nature of Jackson's injury, and Minter didn't know yet if it will be season-ending.

Jackson injured on first play from injury return

Jackson took contact on his hand after his first pass of the game and was in immediate pain. He left the field and walked straight to the locker room. Huntley took his place at quarterback.

The Ravens quickly ruled Jackson out and were down to third-string emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano before halftime after backup Tyler Huntley left with a toe injury in the second quarter.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported postgame that Huntley's injury is believed to be turf toe. His prognosis isn't clear, and he'll have an MRI on Monday to further assess the injury and his timeline to return. The Ravens play the Jaguars Thursday night.

Huntley led Baltimore's offense through the first quarter before he was sidelined early in the second with his toe injury that he sustained on a tackle. The Ravens initially listed him as questionable to return before ruling him out at halftime.

Fagnano took over Baltimore's offense with Buffalo holding a 13-7 lead and finished the game. Fagnano is an undrafted rookie out of Connecticut who signed with Baltimore as a free agent. He completed 10 of 21 passes for 91 yards with 1 interception and no touchdowns.

Fagnano had never played an NFL snap prior to Sunday and was not active Sunday, but listed as Baltimore's emergency quarterback. Per NFL rules, Huntley would have been permitted to return to the game if he was medically cleared, but that point was moot when he got ruled out prior to the third quarter.

Jackson returned to the Baltimore sideline after halftime in street clothes and with a brace on his injured thumb.

A two-time NFL MVP, Jackson was playing in his first game since sustaining a high-ankle sprain in Week 4 that caused him to miss three games. He returned to the 4-3 Ravens in time for the critical AFC showdown against Josh Allen and the Bills, but is now facing another extended absence.

The injury is another difficult blow for Jackson and a Ravens team seeking to compete for a Super Bowl championship. Jackson is one of the game's best players when healthy, but injuries have derailed his last two seasons.

Jackson missed four games last season and was limited in several others with leg and back injuries. The Ravens were projected last season as a Super Bowl contender but finished 8-9 and missed the playoffs.

The Ravens again were projected to compete for a Super Bowl this season, but will be in a fight just to make the playoffs at 4-4 with Jackson injured. And they don't know when Huntley will be able to return.

Jackson, 29, is playing on the fourth year of a five-year, $260 million contract. Team owner Steve Bisciotti has expressed his desire to make Jackson a Raven for life, but the two sides reportedly haven't engaged in substantial contract negotiations .

articles.title: NFL Week 8 Winners and Losers: Lamar Jackson's thumb injury could lead to a sad ending for him and Ravens
articles.summary: The Ravens could be without their quarterback for a while due to another injury.
articles.body:
It's stunning to think that the Baltimore Ravens could have almost a decade of one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time and not make the Super Bowl once. But it might be headed that way.

The Lamar Jackson era was summed up fairly well Sunday. Jackson was back from an ankle injury. The two-time MVP's return brought hope that he could lift the Ravens back to being a Super Bowl contender, starting with a win at the Buffalo Bills. One offensive play in, all that hope was gone.

Jackson suffered a thumb injury following through on a pass on the Ravens' first play on offense. He went to the locker room and was ruled out shortly after. After the game, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Jackson needs surgery and will go to injured reserve , which puts him out at least four weeks. Minter didn't rule out Jackson missing the rest of the season.

Jackson was on the sideline for the second half with a black brace on his right hand. By the time he returned to the sideline he was watching undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano make his NFL debut, after Tyler Huntley left with a toe injury. Baltimore fell to 4-4 with a 36-10 loss to the Bills . Normally a .500 record at the beginning of November wouldn't be the end of anyone's season but it seems like it for Baltimore after Sunday. The Ravens' defense tried to keep the team in the game for as long as it could but there was simply no offense without Jackson. That will be the case going forward as Jackson sits out.

By the time Jackson is back, the Ravens might be well out of the AFC North race.

And if it was just one game against the Bills, or even a few weeks going forward, the mood might be different. But it's way more than that. Jackson is in his ninth season with the Ravens, and the dream of an exciting era having a satisfying conclusion might be fading fast.

Jackson has one year left on a five-year, $260 million contract extension. Multiple media reports have said there have been no recent negotiations. Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti said in January he didn't want the contract issue dragging into April, and now it's November. Both sides have said they want the relationship to continue but it's way more complicated than it was when Jackson was given the franchise tag in 2023 and he came back on a huge deal.

Jackson will turn 30 in January. Injuries are becoming a big part of his story. Given how much he relies on his mobility, his game might not age well into his 30s. There was also a scathing piece by the Baltimore Sun after last season that reshaped the Jackson narrative, painting him as a player who is difficult to work with. Everything is more convoluted with Jackson's future than it was a few years ago. It's especially hard to navigate because of how good Jackson is. He's a three-time first-team All-Pro, entered Sunday's games second all-time in passer rating while also being the greatest running quarterback ever.

The Ravens can entertain trading him — if they don't want to go forward with Jackson after 2027 they'd have to make that move to recoup some value — but everyone knows the chances of finding a quarterback who can be as good as Jackson are almost zero. Seeing Baltimore struggle with Huntley and Fagnano at quarterback gives the Ravens a look at what the future could be without Jackson, and the floor is very low. But if this season goes south, it seems more and more likely that a divorce is on the table next offseason.

The story of this season hasn't been written yet. Assuming Jackson returns, there's a chance to set up a totally different ending with an unlikely playoff berth and postseason run. And, perhaps he and the Ravens simply come to a contract extension like they did last time. It's not like the Ravens have a succession plan in place. But with one play in Buffalo on Sunday, Jackson's future with the Ravens, what comes next for Baltimore and the ripple effects of those decisions around the NFL became the focus. It seemed like a turning point, and not a good one for anyone involved.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 8 of the NFL season:

The 6-2 Pittsburgh Steelers: The Steelers started the season by squeezing out close wins. As the weeks go on, they're starting to look better.

The Cleveland Browns are not the litmus test, despite their 5-2 record coming into Sunday. Cleveland still has a bad quarterback situation and can't live off last-second wins all season. Still, Pittsburgh left no doubt, which is the sign of a good team. The Steelers blasted the Browns 27-6.

Everything was positive. The Steelers' defense played very well. The running game was fantastic again with Jaylen Warren leading the way. Aaron Rodgers was efficient during a game in which he didn't need to do much. The Steelers have a sterling record and are getting better. That's a sign of good coaching. Mike McCarthy is off to a fine start to his Pittsburgh career.

Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers played like a service academy team Sunday, giving up on the passing game altogether in the rain. It was OK because Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell were fantastic in a 16-0 win over the Atlanta Falcons . The Buccaneers didn't complete a pass, but Irving had 170 rushing yards and a touchdown, and Gainwell added 140 more.

it was the first time since 1974 that a team won without a completion. The Buffalo Bills pulled that off in the rain and heavy wind with Joe Ferguson going 0-for-2 passing.

There were completions to Buccaneers, but they came from Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr., who threw four interceptions. Penix struggled in the conditions, while the Buccaneers largely didn't even try to throw it.

The running game was enough for the Buccaneers' second straight win. The NFC South is bad again, so even a team that started 1-5 and has completed fewer than 10 passes the past two weeks should still have hope of winning the division.

Kirk Cousins: Every week, Cousins might be playing for his job. After the Las Vegas Raiders had a four-game losing streak it seemed like a change could be made. Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said last Sunday everything would be considered, including a quarterback change, though he walked that back the next day.

Cousins will keep his job at least another week. He played very well, throwing for three touchdowns and getting another on a quarterback sneak as the Raiders beat the New York Jets 38-33 on Sunday. The Raiders allowed the Jets to score on their first six possessions, but their offense was good enough to overcome that. Cousins was very good, and smart in targeting Brock Bowers repeatedly. Bowers had 92 yards and two touchdowns.

Cousins even got in a celebration after the touchdown, though he looked very much like a 38-year-old quarterback doing it.

At some point this season, top overall draft pick Fernando Mendoza is very likely to start. But it won't be right away, after Cousins had a superb game.

Brian Schottenheimer and Christian Parker: The Dallas Cowboys are in trouble. Their coaching staff might be too.

The Arizona Cardinals, who benched Jacoby Brissett for Gardner Minshew late in the third quarter, came storming back to beat the Cowboys 33-30 in overtime . The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter. Schottenheimer's job security as head coach will be a big topic after the loss. Parker being fired or demoted from his defensive coordinator position seems to be an inevitability even if it doesn't happen right away.

The Cardinals won despite missing a go-ahead extra point with six seconds left. They shook that off, even after having to punt to start overtime. Dak Prescott and his offense failed to score and Dallas' defense couldn't get a stop as Arizona beat Dallas.

It's a horrific loss for the Cowboys and could have long-ranging ramifications. Parker's defense has been awful. It gave up 467 yards even with the Cardinals changing quarterbacks after almost three quarters. The unit gave up four plays of 27 or more yards in the second half, including Tyler Allgeier's 63-yard rushing score.

Minshew had 188 yards and three touchdowns despite not coming in until late in the third quarter. Schottenheimer's offense was inconsistent again too, and the 3-5 record reflects directly on him as a head coach.

The Cowboys have been hesitant to make changes despite a very disappointing start. It might be too much to ignore after one of the worst losses of the NFL season.

Cincinnati Bengals' defense, even in a win: The old problems with Cincinnati's defense are back.

The group hasn't been terrible most of the season but it was Sunday. The Tennessee Titans, who were 32nd in total yardage and 31st in scoring offense entering Sunday, did whatever it wanted against the Bengals. The Titans had 440 yards and scored 36 points.

The Bengals were lucky that Joe Burrow, who had his issues with three interceptions, bailed out the defense . Burrow put together a game-tying drive late in regulation and a rare good play by the defense, when Dexter Lawrence II sacked Cam Ward, sent the game to overtime. Burrow ran for a touchdown and the lead to begin overtime. Then Cincinnati got the stop it needed to finish a 43-36 win. Burrow had five passing touchdowns and another one rushing.

Even though the Bengals pulled it out, a team that gives up 36 points at home to the Titans is tough to trust. Maybe it was just a bad game for a defense that has been OK this season. But, given the Bengals' poor recent history on defense, it's fine to be concerned.

Jonathan Taylor: The Indianapolis Colts probably should have deactivated Taylor on Sunday. There wasn't much point in playing him.

The Colts are in for a rough finish to the season. After trading guard Quenton Nelson and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner earlier in the week, the Colts were wholly uncompetitive in a 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars . They trailed 28-0 at halftime. It's the kind of loss that could lead the team to fire head coach Shane Steichen, even if it was seemingly trying to get through the rest of the season with him. The effort from the defense on multiple Jaguars touchdowns was severely lacking. It was an embarrassing performance for the entire franchise.

Taylor is the one big trade piece left, and the story will unfold one of two ways before the deadline: Taylor's fantastic career with the Colts will come to an end with the team in tatters, or he'll continue to play with a club that might win only a game or two the rest of the season.

For Taylor's sake he will get dealt because the rest of the Colts' season will be depressing.

Vikings' offense: Finally, the Minnesota Vikings' defense couldn't save the day.

The Vikings should have been able to score plenty against a questionable Detroit Lions defense. They put up only 15 points.

Minnesota's defense held strong until Jameson Williams scored a go-ahead touchdown in the final five minutes, and the Vikings couldn't answer. Detroit won 19-15, meaning there are no undefeated teams left this season .

The Vikings have been great on defense and questionable on offense all season. It didn't matter for the first six games, which were all wins. Kyler Murray wasn't the problem Sunday but he wasn't great either, with 210 passing yards against a defense that has been giving up a ton of points and yards this season. At some point if the Vikings want to win the NFC North they'll need some more offensive punch. It's still lacking. And it will really get uncomfortable in Minnesota if J.J. McCarthy, whom they traded a few weeks ago, continues to play well with the Giants.

articles.title: Gardner Minshew leads Cardinals back to stunning win vs. Cowboys after replacing Jacoby Brissett
articles.summary: Gardner Minshew brought the Cardinals all the way back in Week 8.
articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys appeared to be in control early in Week 8. After jumping out to a 17-3 lead, the Cowboys watched as the Arizona Cardinals made a desperation move, benching Jacoby Brissett near the end of the third quarter.

Despite a 14-point deficit, the backup led the Cardinals all the way back against the Cowboys, eventually willing his team to a 33-30 overtime win vs. Dallas.

After leading the team to four straight touchdown drives to tie things up in reguation, Minshew then watched as the Cardinals' defense and running game put the team in position for a game-winning field goal in overtime.

Despite missing an extra point at the end of the fourth quarter that would have won the Cardinals the game in regulation, Cardinals kicker Chad Ryland managed to convert this time, leading the Cardinals to a victory.

It was an improbable result, especially considering how things started. When Minshew took over, his team faced a 14-point deficit, and had not been able to get anything going offensively.

But the backup found a way to rally the Cardinals in the final quarter, bringing the team all the way back to tie the game with just seconds to play. If not for a missed extra-point attempt with just six seconds on the clock, Minshew would have led the Cardinals to a win in regulation.

But Ryland's missed kick kept the game tied. Two plays later, the Cowboys decided to take a knee, sending the contest into overtime.

In overtime, the Cardinals initially gave Minshew a chance to keep the magic going. But a sack and two incomplete passes ended the team's first drive in the frame.

The Cardinals' defense forced a quick stop, however, leading to a 3-and-out for Dallas.

At that point, Arizona decided to bully Dallas' run defense. Minshew completed a short pass to tight end Trey McBride on the team's second drive in overtime and then watched as the Cardinals ran six straight running plays to get into field goal position.

Ryland converted this time around, giving the Cardinals an unexpected win.

That result didn't seem possible through the first three quarters of the contest. With the Cardinals trailing by 14, Brissett couldn't do enough to lead the team back. After taking sacks on consecutive plays with a little over four minutes to play in the third quarter, Brissett was benched in favor of Minshew.

At the time he was removed from the game, Brissett was just 10 of 23 for 119 yards and an interception. He was sacked four times.

With the team trailing 17-3, Minshew was put into the game with roughly 1:35 to play in the third quarter. He completed his first pass attempt and then watched as Tyler Allgeier broke free for a 63-yard rushing touchdown on the next play, bringing the Cardinals within one score.

The Cowboys scored a touchdown on the team's next drive, however, threatening to end any chance of a Cardinals' comeback.

But Minshew continued to claw the team back. Despite the deficit, Minshew threw touchdowns on the team's next two offensive drives. The Cowboys answered both drives with field goals, giving Dallas a 30-24 lead with just 1:06 to play.

Despite being out of timeouts, Minshew once again led the Cardinals down the field, connecting with Allgeier and Michael Wilson to get the team down to the 13-yard line with just 10 seconds to play.

That's when Minshew found Wilson in the back of the end zone for the game-tying touchdown. That proved to be Minshew's final big play in the win, and the one that will likely lead to Minshew being the team's starter moving forward.

After Brissett failed to get things done early, Minshew finished 17 of 23, with 188 passing yards and three touchdowns in the win.

articles.title: Joe Burrow overcomes Amani Hooker's 3 interceptions to lead Bengals to OT win over Titans
articles.summary: Joe Burrow had six total touchdowns to lead the Bengals to their 43-36 win over the Titans.
articles.body:
Amani Hooker pulled off the hat trick on Sunday afternoon.

Yet somehow, that wasn't enough to shake Joe Burrow.

Despite throwing three interceptions to the same defensive back, Burrow still managed to lead the Cincinnati Bengals to a wild 43-36 overtime win against the Tennessee Titans. Burrow threw five touchdowns in the afternoon, and ran in a sixth in the extra period to seal the victory.

Hooker, meanwhile, is now the first player to record three interceptions in a single game since Jordan Whitehead did with the New York Jets in 2023.

Hooker's first interception came in the opening quarter after Burrow launched a ball deep for Ja'Marr Chase. The pass was way off the mark, though, and Hooker was really the only player in the area after Chase cut the wrong way.

Then, after the Bengals took a one-point lead into halftime, Hooker picked Burrow off again on just the fourth play of the third quarter. Burrow tried to hit Mike Gesicki deep, but Hooker was there to jump in front of it.

Unfortunately for the Titans, they fumbled it away two plays later after Cam Ward was drilled in the backfield. That led to a 17-yard touchdown pass to Tee Higgins, which put the Bengals up 21-13 at the time.

Hooker then got his third and final pick near the end of the third quarter. Burrow again tried to find Chase deep, but Hooker cut it off and came up with the easy interception.

Hooker entered the weekend with three interceptions on the season. The former Iowa star, who the Titans selected in the fourth round of the 2019 draft, has now doubled that total.

Despite his bond with Hooker, Burrow threw an 18-yard touchdown pass to Higgins late in the fourth quarter to tie the game. He then ran in a 9-yard score himself in overtime to secure the win.

Ward went 26 of 40 for 304 yards with two touchdowns in the loss for the Titans. Tony Pollard had two scores and 117 yards on 21 carries, and Gunnar Helm had 76 yards on five catches. While that was undoubtedly Ward's best game of the fall — the former Miami star's touchdowns and passing yards were both career-highs — the Titans now sit at just 1-7 on the season.

Burrow went 38 of 48 for 462 yards with five touchdowns and his three interceptions in the win, which pushed Cincinnati to 5-2 on the year. Higgins ended with 155 yards and two touchdowns on 10 catches, and Chase had 141 yards and a score on 11 catches. The Bengals will take on the Atlanta Falcons next week in Madrid.

While it wasn't a perfect day by any means — and he made things more chaotic than they probably needed to be — Burrow got the job done and led Cincinnati to the win. That's all that mattered.

articles.title: Daniel Jones' Future as Colts QB1 Addressed By HC After Being Benched for Anthony Richardson in Loss
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts are officially a mess.

The Indianapolis Colts are officially a mess.

On Sunday, after trading away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, the team was walloped by the Jacksonville Jaguars, 42-7. And Jones' starting position is no longer guaranteed, as head coach Shane Steichen hinted:
