articles.title: Ashton Jeanty's Reduced Role Addressed By Raiders' Klint Kubiak After Win vs. Jets
articles.summary: Las Vegas Raiders second-year running back Ashton Jeanty had his snaps decreased significantly against the New York Jets on Sunday, with Mike Washington Jr. getting the bulk of the work in the backfield.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders second-year running back Ashton Jeanty had his snaps decreased significantly against the New York Jets on Sunday, with Mike Washington Jr. getting the bulk of the work in the backfield.

After the game, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak addressed Jeanty's decreased role.

"That's my call, and Ashton still going to be a big part of our team," Kubiak told reporters .

Kubiak added that the comments Jeanty made about the Jets earlier this week weren't a factor in his decreased reps.

"I think we can definitely get the run game going, get back on track, just really get after this guys," Jeanty told reporters before facing the Jets. "Couple of guys out there that don't really want to tackle, but I'm not going to say names."

Jeanty said it was "communicated" to him before the game that he would get fewer carries.

"We won. It doesn't matter how I feel about how [many] times I get the ball," he told reporters . "Whatever it takes for the team to win, I just want to win. That's all."

Jeanty had just two carries on the day, the fewest he's received in a game since being drafted by the Raiders. He was still active in the passing game, hauling in three catches for 64 yards in the 38-33 win.

Washington took over as the Raiders' RB1 for the day, picking up 83 rushing yards on 25 carries.

Jeanty has had a decent season, but perhaps hasn't played as well as the Raiders hoped he would. Whether he'll go back to being the top option in the backfield next week remains to be seen.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Addresses Brian Schottenheimer Hot Seat Rumors After Cowboys' Loss vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones discussed head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job security following the team's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones discussed head coach Brian Schottenheimer's job security following the team's 33-30 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday.

Jones told reporters that he wasn't thinking about a coaching change after the game.

The Cowboys fell to 3-5 with the defeat, as they've now lost three of their past four games.

Jones was also noncommittal when asked if he had any concerns about Schottenheimer not getting things done.

"Well, I don't know," Jones said, per Calvin Watkins of the Dallas Morning News . "None of us are getting it done and that should be my concern. So I'm not pointing at Schotty, I'm not pointing to anybody, but none of us have it done. I haven't been involved in too many games that we should have wanted and we had the opportunities we had to win this game. So that is a big snapshot that we want to put above our mirror."

The Cowboys struggled early on offense against Arizona, but were still able to take a 14-3 lead at halftime before extending their advantage to 17-3 in the third quarter.

Dallas appeared to be headed towards a win after the Cardinals benched starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett near the end of the third, but backup passer Gardner Minshew entered the game and helped Arizona outscore the Cowboys 27-13 throughout the remainder of regulation.

Still, the Cowboys gained some momentum after the Cardinals missed a potential game-winning extra point and were forced to punt on the first drive of overtime.

The excitement was short-lived, as Dallas lost five yards on three plays before punting the ball back to Arizona.

The Cardinals kicked a 42-yard field goal on their final drive, securing the victory.

It was a particularly disappointing performance from the Cowboys, as they were facing the backup quarterback of an Arizona squad that ranked No. 26 among all teams by averaging just 20.3 points per game heading into Sunday's action.

Schottenheimer may not be in danger of losing his job just yet, but his seat is getting hotter.

articles.title: Chiefs Kingdom surprised Jason Kelce as $14.90 donation campaign helped his charity surpass $100,000 fundraising goal
articles.summary: In 2023, a Super Bowl rivalry between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles sparked an unexpected show of generosity.
articles.body: In 2023, a Super Bowl rivalry between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles sparked an unexpected show of generosity. Even after watching their team defeat Philadelphia on the biggest stage in football, Chiefs fans found a reason to celebrate an Eagles star. Jason Kelce became the recipient of their kindness, thanks to a simple idea shared by a Chiefs fan page. What followed was a fundraising effort that crossed team loyalties and brought rival supporters together for a cause much bigger than football. The response also gave Jason's charitable work a remarkable boost.Chiefs Kingdom turns Super Bowl victory into a charitable gestureThe story began after Kansas City defeated Philadelphia in Super Bowl LVII. While Chiefs fans celebrated their team's victory, one supporter group decided to direct some of that excitement towards Jason Kelce and his charitable organisation, the Be Philly Foundation.A Chiefs fan page on Twitter encouraged supporters to donate $14.90 to the foundation. The amount carried a special meaning, combining the jersey numbers of the Kelce brothers. Travis wears No. 87 for Kansas City, while Jason wore No. 62 for Philadelphia.Rather than allowing the Super Bowl rivalry to define the relationship between the two fanbases, the campaign offered a different message. Fans could celebrate Travis' championship while supporting something meaningful to Jason and his community.The idea quickly gained attention, with donations pouring in from people associated with the Chiefs Kingdom. It was a reminder that the connections created by football can extend far beyond the field.Jason Kelce's Be Philly Foundation thanks Chiefs fans after crossing $100,000The response exceeded the foundation's expectations. On Thursday, February 16, 2023, the Be Philly Foundation publicly acknowledged the generosity of Chiefs supporters after its online fundraising campaign crossed the initial $100,000 target.The organisation highlighted where much of the support had come from, making the gesture even more meaningful."Largely coming from our opponents last Sunday, we have now exceeded our initial online fundraising goal of $100,000," the charity said in a post. "Chiefs Kingdom sure knows how to win with class, and I cannot thank you all enough for supporting the (Be)Philly Foundation’s mission here in Philadelphia. As a reminder, 100% of donations go directly towards funding our selected programs."The foundation also stressed that every donation would go directly towards its selected programmes. That assurance gave supporters a clear understanding of how their contributions would be used.For Jason, the campaign offered a heartwarming example of how his brother's supporters were willing to stand behind his charitable work. The gesture also showed that NFL rivalries do not have to end in hostility. articles.title: Anthony Richardson Opens Up on Scary Eye Injury in Video After Replacing Daniel Jones in Colts' Loss
articles.summary: Anthony Richardson played in his first game since suffering a scary eye injury on Sunday, and the Indianapolis Colts quarterback addressed just how serious his injury was after the game.
articles.body:
Anthony Richardson played in his first game since suffering a scary eye injury on Sunday, and the Indianapolis Colts quarterback addressed just how serious his injury was after the game.

"I would go to the doctor, and they would tell me they don't know if I'm getting my vision back and stuff like that," he told reporters. "I'm just grateful that I even get the chance to go out there and throw a pass, regardless of if I step on the field or not, cause there was a day and a time where this wasn't promised for me."

Last October, Richardson was warming up with elastic bands when the equipment he had them tied to malfunctioned and hit him in the face. He suffered an orbital fracture , forcing him to miss the rest of the season.

He didn't regain full vision in his eye until February.

Getting back onto the field is a huge step for Richardson, even if he only played a handful of snaps. Richardson, the former No. 4 overall pick in 2022, completed both of his pass attempts for eight yards in a 42-7 blowout loss to the Jaguars. He replaced starter Daniel Jones late in the game when it was already out of reach.

Richardson's return to action comes at a time when the starting job in Indianapolis is very much in flux. Jones has had a rough campaign after his breakout season last year, throwing for 1,542 yards, five touchdowns and nine interceptions.

Head coach Shane Steichen made it clear after the game that he plans to consider making a change under center.

"I'm gonna evaluate everything," Steichen told reporters after the game. "Every position going forward."

Richardson has had a rough start to his career, missing almost all of his rookie year before struggling in Year 2 and failing to earn the starting job last season. Perhaps he'll get another chance to prove himself as Indianapolis searches for answers.

The Colts dropped to 2-6 with the loss as the playoffs continue to get more out of reach for them.

articles.title: The last undefeated NFL team in 2026 has lost
articles.summary: Eight weeks into the NFL season, there are no longer any undefeated teams.  The Detroit Lions’ 19-15 win Sunday over Minnesota ended the Vikings’ (6-1) unbeaten start.
articles.body: Eight weeks into the NFL season, there are no longer any undefeated teams. The Detroit Lions’ 19-15 win Sunday over Minnesota ended the Vikings’ (6-1) unbeaten start. Minnesota’s loss also ended its 11-game winning streak in the regular season, dating to last season, which was the NFL’s longest active streak. A win Sunday would have tied the franchise’s longest all-time win streak from 1969. The Vikings trailed 12-7 entering the fourth quarter after a 30-yard run by Lions running back Jahmyr Gibbs, the NFL’s leader in touchdowns. Minnesota took back the lead with 3:56 to play in the fourth quarter when T.J. Hockensen’s eight-yard touchdown pass from Kyler Murray was followed by a successful two-point conversion for a 15-12 advantage. Detroit scored the go-ahead touchdown four minutes later, after a long drive was ended by a 7-yard touchdown catch by Jameson Williams. Minnesota’s attempt to take the lead back ended meekly, after their next possession lasted just three plays and traveled five yards before a punt. Offensive struggles have plagued the Vikings all season. Despite their 6-0 start, they entered Sunday ranked in the bottom third of the league in scoring average and their 281 yards per game ranked fourth-fewest. “I don’t necessarily think right now off the top of my head it’s one particular thing,” Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said of his team’s offensive inconsistencies after gaining 266 yards and 15 first downs, nine fewer than Detroit. “We’re just looking for consistent. Doesn’t need to be much more than guys doing their jobs. Pitching and catching.” They had relied on a defense that had blitzed on 70.8% of opportunities through six weeks, on pace for the highest percentage since Next Gen Stats began tracking blitzes in 2016. The Vikings blitzed Lions quarterback Jared Goff at an even higher rate of 89.7%, on 26 of his 29 dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats. Goff did throw an interception against the blitz, but also completed a touchdown and threw for 130 yards because Minnesota’s blitzes were often successfully picked up by Detroit blockers. Minnesota’s defense also did not have an answer for Gibbs, who forced 12 missed tackles en route to 153 yards on the ground. The game was paused for roughly five minutes during the second half when Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was injured while making a tackle and laid on the turf, unmoving. He was carted off the field, taken to a local hospital and evaluated for a neck injury, according to the team. “He’s being taken care of, we don’t have any new information,” Lions coach Dan Campbell said. “We’re thinking about him.”

articles.title: Michael Wilson Injured, Cardinals WR Gives Status Update After Game-Tying TD vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Michael Wilson made the play of the day in the Arizona Cardinals' win over the Dallas Cowboys despite dealing with a serious injury.
articles.body:
Michael Wilson made the play of the day in the Arizona Cardinals' win over the Dallas Cowboys despite dealing with a serious injury.

The wide receiver made the game-tying touchdown grab, and the Cardinals went on to win in overtime. He revealed after the game that he had two broken ribs.

"This organization's paying me a lot of money," he said. "So if I can muster up the strength to go play, even at 60 percent, I'm going to."

Wilson told reporters after the game that he was dealing with sore ribs after last week's game against the Denver Broncos, and he was later diagnosed with broken ribs.

Despite a serious injury, Wilson finished the day with 111 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions, marking his best game of the season so far.

"I'm ecstatic that we won, but physically, not too good," Wilson said . "... Pain is temporary, glory is forever. I'll take the rib pain for a win for the Arizona Cardinals."

The question now is whether Wilson will be able to play again next week. After making the game-tying catch, he appeared to be in some pain as he walked to the bench, but perhaps he'll be able to recover fully over the next week.

The Cardinals have had a rough season for the most part, but have managed to pick up a few quality wins. They likely aren't expecting to make a playoff run, but they could still end up having a respectable season.

"When stuff is s--tty, that's when you can really find out who you are as a person, who you are as a man, but also about your teammates," Wilson said. "I could not be more proud to be an Arizona Cardinal under a team led by Mike LaFleur."

Wilson's grittiness to go out and play despite two broken ribs could end up lighting a fire under his teammates heading into the rest of the year.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs denies wrongdoing after abuse allegations by 3 other women following May arrest
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs missed six games this season while on the commissioner's exempt list following his arrest in May.
articles.body:
Josh Jacobs has denied any wrongdoing after three other women contacted police to report abuse allegations against him while the Green Bay Packers running back was being investigated for a different incident earlier this year.

Jacobs' attorneys issued a statement on Sunday afternoon denying all three additional abuse allegations that were made against him, and said that he has "a substantial body of tangible evidence to back up his assertions."

"The three accounts are old, are hearsay and easily disproven, yet released to the media by police without any investigation to determine whether they were accurate or contradicted by evidence," his attorneys said, via the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. "Josh is answering them in detail because of the character assassination that is occurring, unfairly threatening his career."

New allegations made against Josh Jacobs

Jacobs was arrested in northern Wisconsin in May and charged with multiple counts of domestic abuse. He allegedly grabbed a woman trying to leave his garage and threw her to the ground. He was formally charged with battery and criminal damage to property after that incident, and he pleaded no contest to both charges.

Jacobs landed on the commissioner's exempt list and missed the first six weeks of the NFL season as a result.

On Saturday, previously unreleased files showed that the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department was contacted by at least three other women accusing Jacobs of abuse in recent years.

One woman told police that, in 2022, Jacobs slapped her in the face and took her cellphone as she tried to leave his home. She told investigators that Jacobs grabbed her by the hair, pinned her down on a bed, threw her onto the floor, spit on her and grabbed her by the throat. The woman said that the two remained friends after the incident, and she didn't want to report him to police. Jacobs' attorneys said that the woman reported it to the league, but that the NFL reviewed it and decided no action was warranted.

A second woman said that, in 2021, Jacobs grabbed her arm, pushed her up against a wall and threw items of hers outside of the home. She said she had swelling by her rib area and suffered bruising to her arms. She contacted police after the incident and said it was not investigated as a domestic incident because the two were not in a relationship. Jacobs' attorneys said that he called Las Vegas police to his home to report the woman for misconduct, and that her claims were "effectively undermined" in a police report.

A third woman said that Jacobs flew her to his home in 2022, and that she had an altercation with Jacobs in which he grabbed her by the head, dragged her, scratched her chest and took her phone after it fell on the floor. The woman said that she had bruising on her arm and scratches on her chest, and that she didn't report it at the time because she feared being deported from the United States.

Jacobs' attorneys said that he denied any physical altercation with the third woman, that another person was present in the house during part of the stay, and that she left the following evening on her own.

"The police department's released file contains only phone interviews, taken years after the fact, with no additional investigation save for an acknowledgement that Josh did nothing wrong," his attorneys said. "Josh was not given an opportunity to present evidence to Hobart-Lawrence in response to the uncorroborated report, primarily because Hobart-Lawrence took no action related to the unsupported and stale allegations."

Regardless of whether Jacobs faces criminal charges from the new allegations, the NFL could still suspend Jacobs for violating the league's personal conduct policy. The NFL said in a statement that it was reviewing "these allegations as part of the investigation which has remained open."

Jacobs returned to play for the Packers in their Week 7 loss to the Detroit Lions. He had 39 rushing yards and a touchdown on 21 carries in their win over the Carolina Panthers on Thursday.

articles.title: NFL: Detroit Lions' Jack Campbell taken to hospital with neck injury
articles.summary: Jack Campbell was placed on a stretcher and carted off the pitch during the Detroit Lions' game on Sunday, before being taken to hospital.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell was taken to hospital to be treated for a neck injury after being hurt during an NFL game against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday.

Campbell's head was struck while tackling tight end TJ Hockenson in the third quarter, and he was face down on the pitch when medical officials rushed to his side.

The 26-year-old was placed on a stretcher and taken off the pitch on a cart to a round of applause after team-mates and most of the Lions coaching staff surrounded him while he received attention.

The Lions confirmed he was transported to hospital.

"Thoughts and prayers are with Jack and his family. He's being taken care of, we don't have any new information," said Lions head coach Dan Campbell.

Jack Campbell - who is not related to the coach - was drafted by the Lions with the number 18 overall pick in 2023 and signed a contract extension in May of this year through to the 2030 season.

Last season, he was an All-Pro selection after becoming the first NFL player in seven years to have 150-plus tackles and at least five sacks and three forced fumbles.

The Lions won Sunday's game 19-15, with Campbell's team-mates DJ Wonnum and Brian Branch both suffering concussions.

articles.title: Jonathan Taylor Says Teams Will Be 'Foaming at the Mouth' to Play Colts Amid 2-6 Record
articles.summary: Star running back Jonathan Taylor believes tougher days await the Indianapolis Colts as they try to dig out of a 2-6 record.
articles.body:
Star running back Jonathan Taylor believes tougher days await the Indianapolis Colts as they try to dig out of a 2-6 record.

"It's not going to get any easier," Taylor told reporters following Sunday's 42-7 loss against the Tennessee Titans. "It's actually going to get even harder. And teams are going to look at as even more like, foaming at the mouth. So then it comes to a point of like, 'Hey, what are you going to do? Your back's against the wall. What are you going to do? You're gonna have to fight your way out of a corner. Like literally, fight your way out of a corner.' And that's all I'm thinking about, for myself but also how to convey that to the rest of the guys in the locker room."

Of course, it remains to be seen how much longer Taylor remains in Indianapolis, with his name popping up in trade rumors. The Colts have already begun the fire sale, and Taylor would be a logical player to move given the draft capital he might demand.

But if he does remain with the team, he knows the task ahead of them is a tall one.

articles.title: Stefon Diggs rocks Allen Iverson jersey before Eagles-Commanders game
articles.summary: Commanders receiver Stefon Diggs arrived for Sunday's game against the Eagles wearing an Allen Iverson 76ers jersey, honoring a Philadelphia icon
articles.body:
Washington Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs brought a touch of Philadelphia basketball history to Sunday night's NFC East matchup against the Eagles , arriving at the stadium wearing a throwback Allen Iverson 76ers jersey.

The Commanders shared Diggs' pregame look on their official social media account ahead of the nationally televised matchup. The veteran receiver's choice of attire connected two cities through one of basketball's most recognizable figures, who became a Philadelphia sports icon after growing up in Virginia and playing college basketball at Georgetown.

Iverson, a native of Hampton, Virginia, attended Georgetown for two seasons before the 76ers selected him with the No. 1 overall pick in the 1996 NBA draft. He became the face of Philadelphia basketball, winning the NBA's Most Valuable Player award in 2001 and leading the Sixers to the NBA Finals that season.

Stefon Diggs pays tribute to Philadelphia sports icon

Iverson remains one of the most celebrated athletes in Philadelphia sports history, earning 11 NBA All-Star selections and four scoring titles during a Hall of Fame career. His influence extended beyond basketball, with his playing style, fashion, and personality helping make him a defining athlete of his generation.

The 76ers retired Iverson's No. 3 jersey in 2014, and he was inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2016. His connection to the Washington region also makes Diggs' choice particularly fitting, given Iverson's Virginia roots and his two standout seasons at Georgetown before entering the NBA.

Diggs also has a connection to the region. The veteran receiver grew up in Maryland, attended Our Lady of Good Counsel High School and played college football at Maryland before entering the NFL as a fifth-round pick of the Minnesota Vikings in 2015.

The four-time Pro Bowl receiver signed with Washington in August, bringing experience and production to an offense built around quarterback Jayden Daniels. His arrival gave the Commanders another established receiving threat as they attempted to compete in the NFC East.

Diggs prepares to face Eagles on Sunday Night Football

The pregame tribute comes before an important divisional matchup for both teams, especially Philadelphia, which entered Sunday at 2-5 after five straight losses. Washington also entered the contest looking to improve its standing in the NFC East, adding significance to a nationally televised game featuring two teams trying to reverse disappointing starts.

Diggs has become an important part of Washington's passing attack, giving Daniels an experienced target who can make plays against tight coverage. Philadelphia counters with a secondary featuring Quinyon Mitchell, Cooper DeJean and Riq Woolen, giving the Eagles several options as defensive coordinator Vic Fangio attempts to limit the Commanders' passing game.

Mitchell entered Week 8 leading qualifying NFL cornerbacks with a 61.8 passer rating allowed, according to the Eagles' weekly game release. The matchup between Washington's receivers and Philadelphia's defensive backs will be particularly important for an Eagles defense that has struggled to consistently generate pressure on opposing quarterbacks.

Diggs' choice of an Iverson jersey provided a memorable pregame moment before the division rivals took the field. The receiver's tribute also reminded fans of Iverson's lasting influence across the region, connecting his Virginia upbringing and Georgetown career with the basketball legacy he built in Philadelphia.

For Eagles fans, seeing an opposing receiver arrive wearing the jersey of one of the city's most beloved athletes added an unexpected Philadelphia connection to Sunday night's matchup.

articles.title: Tom Brady Accidentally Curses During Live“ ”Broadcast for the Second Time This Year
articles.summary: The Fox Sports lead NFL analyst made a similar on-air slip while reacting to Jayden Daniels’ injury in September
articles.body:
Tom Brady accidentally cursed during a live Fox NFL Sunday broadcast for the second time this year

Brady blurted out the expletive after incorrectly naming Drew Brees during a Fox NFL Sunday quiz on Nov. 1

The Fox analyst made a similar on-air slip while reacting to Jayden Daniels' injury during a live broadcast in September

Tom Brady dropped a swear word on live TV — just about a month after he made headlines for using the same curse word during another broadcast.

The 49-year-old NFL alum and sports announcer said " Oh, s---" during a live Fox NFL Sunday broadcast on Sunday, Nov. 1. The moment came as Brady fumbled a response during a "Who's in Third?" quiz with fellow quarterback-turned-broadcaster Drew Brees .

As the Fox Sports lead NFL analyst and Brees, 47, did the quiz about which quarterback ranks in third place in different all-time league achievements, the New England Patriots legend accidentally answered the final question with Brees — despite Brees already being on the list in No. 1.

Asked who has the third most career games with more than 300 passing yards behind Brees and himself in first and second place, respectively, Brady said, "Drew Brees!" which he then immediately followed up with, "Oh, s---!"

As Brady accidentally blurted out the expletive he looked off-camera slightly. He then quickly turned back, seemingly upon realizing that he'd sworn on the air, and appeared to say, "Ope."

The analyst's eyes also went wide and he put his hands out in front of his face in the aftermath of the accidental on-air expletive.

Brady, Brees and the rest of the Fox NFL Sunday laughed off his gaffe as Peyton Manning was revealed to be the correct answer to the final question of the quarterback quiz.

Brady's Week 8 cursing during the Nov. 1 broadcast comes over a month after he first accidentally blurted out a swear word on-air during Week 2.

The first "oh, s---" was a reaction to Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels ' serious left elbow injury, which he suffered in the first half of the team's Week 2 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys on Sept. 20.

As a replay of the injury was shown on Fox's broadcast, Brady couldn't help but share a genuine reaction. During the live broadcast, he questioned if a player's "foot came over" before Daniels suffered the injury and said, "Was that a center? [Nick] Allegretti — oh, s---."

Brady then immediately realized his live blunder and said, "Excuse me," before telling viewers that he was "not expecting to see that."

The former Patriots quarterback made his debut on Fox Sports in 2024. He has faced criticism for his broadcasting skills since — including recently, for making a series of critical comments regarding the officiating in the Lions-Packers game, which could lead him to face major fees .

Brady, who is a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders, could be found in violation of the "Brady Rules" broadcasting agreement, which the NFL established due to Brady's desire to work in the broadcasting booth while also helping to oversee the Raiders — and which comes with a $500,000 first-time violation fine.

But Brady recently told Sports Business Journal he's not concerned with his critics. " It's clickbait for people, and it's something that people have no idea what they're really glomming onto," he told the outlet in the interview ahead of his third season in the booth.

"They just put it out there in the world and see what sticks," Brady said. "So to me, I just focus on what I need to do to be prepared. That's what I did as a player, and I go out there every week as a broadcaster and try to do the same thing."

The former quarterback admitted he still has "a lot to prove to myself, my teammates," as well as "the executives," but said he's eager to find his way. "I want to go earn it," he told Sports Business Journal, "and I don't want anything given to me. I hope they'll have me through the end of this contract. I love getting to enjoy the game. I love watching good football."

articles.title: An NFL team just won a game without completing a pass. No, seriously.
articles.summary: Facing the Atlanta Falcons in a game played amid a downpour, the Tampa By Buccaneers attempted only three passes. And won.
articles.body: The offense run by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday was the most predictable of the 2026 NFL season. Facing the Atlanta Falcons in a key divisional matchup of Week 8, during a game played amid a downpour that left standing water pooling on the field inside Raymond James Stadium, the Buccaneers attempted only three passes, completing none. Unwilling and unable to throw in soggy conditions, they ran it 56 times. The strategy won them the game, 16-0. “First time for everything,” Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said. To say it was an unusual game plan was an understatement. The last time an NFL team had more rushing attempts than Tampa’s 56 was 2010. The Buccaneers were the first team to win without a completed pass since Buffalo in 1974, per the league. Rarer still was that a team hadn’t won by double-digits without completing a pass since 1945, according to one NFL researcher. The Buccaneers had been forced to rely on a ground-heavy offense last week, as well, when quarterback Baker Mayfield threw only 11 times in his first game back since suffering a thumb injury. Tampa had rushed for 258 yards in that win against Carolina, then leaned on a similar plan Sunday as the forecast showed a storm rolling over Florida. Nearly an inch of rain had fallen over Tampa by kickoff, and the rain didn’t stop as the game began. Mayfield finished 0-3 passing, but was all smiles after the game, considering it was Tampa’s first home win this season after an 0-4 start. Did Bowles tell Tampa Bay’s offensive coordinator not to pass? “We didn’t say you’re not going to throw the ball; the conditions told him that,” Bowles said. “You could see it’s a downpour down there and the wind’s blowing. You can kind of see the ball’s not going anywhere.” Against the Falcons, Tampa Bay gained a franchise-record 324 yards on the ground, an average of 5.8 yards per rush, as the backfield tandem of Bucky Irving (170 yards) and Kenny Gainwell (140) repeatedly ran through Atlanta’s defense. Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix Jr. completed just 8-of-24 passes and was intercepted four times and fumbled once. It was a marked difference from Penix’s last two games, in which he’d thrown for six touchdowns and zero interceptions combined. Mayfield fumbled three times, though he didn’t lose any. Irving did lose a fumble. “It’s a win so,” Mayfield said. “I’ll take it, man.”

articles.title: Jerry Jones is fed up with the Cowboys. But will he do anything about it?
articles.summary: A brutal collapse left the Cowboys and their owner scrambling for answers.
articles.body:
Most times when TV cameras cut to a team's owner, we get an unremarkable shot of a billionaire celebrating with a collection of family, employees and assorted hangers-on. It's an annoying but nearly-mandatory backrub for the NFL's ruling class.

And then there's Jerry Jones. Every time the cameras cut to him, buddy, you know you're in for a ride, particularly when his team saws off its own foot the way it did Sunday in an overtime loss to the Cardinals.

Oh, was Jerry angry. There was the disbelieving "gotta be kidding me" when the Cardinals frog-marched the Cowboys backwards down the field and lined up for the game-tying touchdown. And the disgusted expletive as the Cardinals vultured away the victory in overtime:

In a single syllable, Jones effectively summed up the 2026 Cowboys. This is a team that began the season with Super Bowl aspirations, a team that's now — per Jones' succinct description — swirling down the toilet.

"We had numerable chances to win this game," Jones said after the game , "and didn't do it."

How long can this continue? A lot longer than Cowboys fans might like. Jones' end-of-game frustration surely mirrors that of Cowboys fans. But unlike those fans, Jones has the power to make changes on this team. And much to the frustration of a growing segment of those Cowboys fans, Jones is choosing not to kick head coach Brian Schottenheimer to the curb. Yet.

"I made a change with Wade Phillips in the middle of the season," Jones said after the game. "I don't see that here." Phillips went 1-7 in 2010 before Jones fired him; his replacement, Jason Garrett, finished the season 5-3.

Why? Well, perhaps because firing Schottenheimer wouldn't do enough to root out the rot that's infecting the organization. "A lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said . "For whatever criticism we want to have of Brian, we can all get in line. That was a total — to use a cliche — total team effort today from us."

What's wrong? Start with the defense, which has dramatically underachieved since Week 1 under new DC Christian Parker. Against Arizona, Dallas had 14-point leads in the third (17-3) and fourth (24-10) quarters. The Cardinals began what would be their decisive drive on their own 20 with 1:09 remaining in the game and no timeouts. Surrendering the game with those kinds of cushions might well qualify as a felony in the state of Texas.

The numbers are indisputable. Dallas has given up at least 20 points in every single game this season. Of the Cowboys' five losses, four were one-possession deficits. Coming into Sunday, only two teams had surrendered more than Dallas' 373.7 yards per game, and Dallas ranked dead last in rushing yards allowed. Twice — against the Ravens and now the Cardinals — the Cowboys have given up the crucial tying or go-ahead score with only a handful of seconds remaining on the clock.

The offense shouldn't escape scrutiny, nor should Schottenheimer. Through a season and a half, Schottenheimer has only one winning streak, and that was only three games, coming in November of last year. For every heroic connection between Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb, there are five inexplicable play calls and inconsistent executions.

These are not the characteristics of a team that exerts its will on either side of the ball. These are the numbers of an overmatched team that opponents are blowing off the field, both physically and psychologically.

The grim irony of this Dallas downfall is that the Cowboys play in an eminently winnable division. Philadelphia has all but waved the white flag, Washington is leaking oil, and New York is patching new holes in the roster every week. If Dallas were even remotely competent, the Cowboys would already be running away with this division.

Instead, they're bumbling around, buried in the standings at 3-5, letting opportunity after opportunity slip away as the season goes to … well, Jerry's got the right word for it .

articles.title: Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce's $200 million Garage Beer has one bizarre secret behind its marketing success
articles.summary: Garage Beer is taking an unconventional route to win over beer drinkers, and Jason Kelce is right at the centre of its strategy.
articles.body: Garage Beer is taking an unconventional route to win over beer drinkers, and Jason Kelce is right at the centre of its strategy. Rather than compete with major brewing companies through expensive advertising, the independent brand is turning ridiculous jokes, unexpected stunts and genuine fan connections into its biggest marketing assets. In March 2026, the company is showing how a distinctive personality can help a smaller business capture attention. Its approach is simple: entertain people first, build a community around the experience and let the brand become part of the conversation.Garage Beer uses Jason Kelce and absurd humour to challenge bigger brandsGarage Beer's latest marketing push arrived ahead of March Madness, with college basketball commentator and lawyer Jay Bilas taking on the fictional role of its 'Attorney at Lager'. The campaign pokes fun at local law firm advertisements, complete with a video commercial and a hotline where fans can leave messages. The brand also introduced a sweepstakes offering a $5,000 TickPick gift card.However, the campaign reflects a much bigger creative strategy. Garage Beer has built its identity around humour that established competitors might hesitate to embrace. Its regional Super Bowl advertisement offered a memorable example, with co-owner Jason Kelce putting horse manure on his face while parodying Budweiser's famous Clydesdale commercials.Chief Creative Officer Corey Smale believes this unconventional approach gives the company an advantage.“Dumb is hard to replicate,” said Garage Beer Chief Creative Officer Corey Smale. “The authenticity that the brand has put out there over the last few years is uniquely ours. We have to stay committed to that.”The company has also introduced a weekly Instagram series called 'Thank Garage It's Friday'. Featuring fictional laboratory experiments, bizarre inventions and mock press conferences, the videos aim to give audiences something entertaining amid the endless stream of social media content.Garage Beer's response to its Super Bowl advertisement also revealed how quickly it can adapt. Although the team expected its toilet humour to attract attention, viewers became more interested in the miniature horse featured in the commercial. The brand responded with merchandise, stickers and a farm experience sweepstakes centred on the animal.Garage Beer builds customer loyalty through community and creativityBeyond social media, Garage Beer is investing in physical merchandise and experiences that bring its online community closer to the brand. Its products are now available across all 50 states, giving the company a wider platform for future launches.Smale also revealed that the brand relies on a small in-house creative team rather than traditional advertising agencies. It has created a private Instagram group for around 5,000 dedicated followers, allowing the company to test ideas and gather reactions before wider releases.One unusual example involved a loyal customer who repeatedly posted about the brand and jokingly asked Garage Beer to buy him a house. Smale sent him $500 through Venmo, and the follower later shared photographs of his new home.The gesture captures the unusual relationship Garage Beer wants with its customers. Instead of treating fans as just another audience, the company wants them to become active supporters who help shape its identity.As the March 2026 campaign demonstrates, Garage Beer is betting that personality, humour and genuine community connections can compete with advertising budgets that smaller brands simply cannot match.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tampa Bay Buccaneers win NFL game without completing a pass, first time that's happened in half a century
articles.summary: Baker Mayfield attempted three passes with zero completions as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers rushed for a club-record 324 yards in a rain-soaked shutout.
articles.body: The joke will be that the Tampa Bay Buccaneers set back the modern-day NFL offense by decades on Sunday by failing to complete even one pass, something which had happened only one other time during the Super Bowl era. But the Bucs get the last laugh. They came away from Sunday's rain-drenched, mud-soaked meeting with the Atlanta Falcons with a 16-0 victory where they set a new club rushing mark of 324 yards. On top of that, they have renewed life in the NFC South. BUCCANEERS COLLECT TWO FREAKISH FIRST-HALF SCORES TO DOMINATE PANTHERS – AND, OH, BAKER MAYFIELD IS BACK Afterward, coach Todd Bowles was asked if he informed his offensive coordinator or quarterback Baker Mayfield they weren't going to throw the ball a lot. "The conditions told him that," Bowles said. "I mean, you could see it as a downpour down there and the wind's blowing. You can kind of see the ball wasn't going anywhere." FALCONS STAR BIJAN ROBINSON WANTS EVERY NFL TEAM TO PLAY INDOORS ONE DAY: 'THAT WOULD BE SICK' So much for the space-age passing inside an air conditioned dome. This was three yards and a cloud of dust. Or rather, because this game at Raymond James Stadium was played in that unrelenting rain, it was three-yards-and-a-lot-of-slush. So, a lot of running football. And, just to be accurate, for way more than three-yards a pop. But no passing. Quarterback Baker Mayfield attempted three passes without a completion. "All right, let's get this over with because you don't want to talk to me," Mayfield told reporters to open his postgame news conference. This was some surreal stuff and that was obvious when Mayfield was asked questions about his lead blocking on one play. "You know, if you're not going to throw the ball, I got to get active somehow," he said. The last and only other time a team failed to complete a pass in a game since the NFL began playing Super Bowls was on Sept. 29, 1974 by the Buffalo Bills, according to the Associated Press. It was O.J. Simpson's Bills that did it that time with quarterback Joe Ferguson attempting only two passes without a completion. Simpson ran for 117 yards in that long-ago game. Bucky Irving and Kenneth Gainwell went bonkers in this game. Irving gained 170 yards and averaged 6.3 yards per carry against the Falcons. Gainwell gained 140 rushing yards and averaged 5.6 yards per attempt. Historic. But Irving didn't see it that way. "I'm not going to lie to you. I don't know the last time I checked the weather for a football game," he said. "We're going to have to play in it anyway. That's how I think about it. "Rain, snow, muddy, you're going to have to play in it anyway." ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW! It could be argued the Bucs would have been more productive, if perhaps, they had tried a pass sometime in the second half. But the Falcons tried doing some of that. Their quarterback, Michael Penix Jr. completed only eight of his 24 attempts, throwing four interceptions. articles.title: Amani Hooker's Contract Bonus Revealed After 3 INTs Off Joe Burrow in Titans' OT Loss vs. Bengals
articles.summary: Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker went off for three interceptions against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, and it landed him a big payday.
articles.body:
Tennessee Titans safety Amani Hooker went off for three interceptions against Joe Burrow and the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, and it landed him a big payday.

Hooker's contract includes a $250,000 bonus if he has at least four interceptions during the season, and he came into Sunday's game with two, so the three-pick day helped him meet the threshold.

If he can record one more this year, it will land him a $500,000 bonus.

Hooker, 28, is on a three-year, $40.5 million deal with the Titans, who drafted him in the fourth round in 2019. With five interceptions already on the season, Hooker has already matched his career high.

Unfortunately for the Titans, Hooker's monster game wasn't enough to get them the win. Tennessee lost 43-36 in overtime, dropping to 1-7 on the year. Things will only get tougher after their upcoming bye as the Titans face the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Jared Verse Calls Out Steelers Player for Viral Video of Slam, Browns DE Trolled After Trash Talk
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns pass-rusher Jared Verse weighed in on the play in which he was slammed to the ground by Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick during Pittsburgh's 27-6 win over Cleveland on Sunday.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns pass-rusher Jared Verse weighed in on the play in which he was slammed to the ground by Pittsburgh Steelers guard Mason McCormick during Pittsburgh's 27-6 win over Cleveland on Sunday.

"I jumped in the air to try to block the kick," Verse told reporters after the game. "He swept my legs in the air, ended up landing on my head. That's football. I'm very upset about it. If this wasn't football, I'd be acting a different way."

"I love football, I love the aggression," he added. "I love how much goes into it, how much we put of our lives into football. But to do something like that, I can't have respect for anything like that."

After the Steelers scored a touchdown in the first quarter of the game, McCormick lifted up Verse and threw him to the ground during the ensuing extra point. The guard received an unnecessary roughness penalty for the play.

Verse, who previously exchanged trash talk with Pittsburgh ahead of the contest, received a response from multiple Steelers players on Sunday.

"He should have kept his mouth shut," safety Jaquan Brisker told reporters following the win. "All that talk, and then to come out with zero tackles, that's bad. You didn't stand behind your words and you didn't stand on business. He's gotta look at himself in the mirror and get better."

Steelers running back Jaylen Warren also said that "some walk, some talk" when asked if Verse gave the team bulletin board material during his press conference .

Verse initially called Pittsburgh "dirty" following a Week 4 matchup between the AFC North rivals.

"They were talking crazy," Verse said at the time, per USA Today's Adam Bittner . "I was telling them, 'Y'all double-teaming and sliding and you're garbage.' I don't have respect for anybody that plays too dirty and does too much extra [stuff] after the game. I can't wait to see them again. It's going to be a great time when I see them again."

Steelers defensive tackle Cameron Heyward eventually reacted to Verse's comments during a Tuesday appearance on The Rich Eisen Show .

"Double teaming, sliding, chipping, are those not allowed in our game?" Heyward said, via Bittner. "Yeah, I got the bruises to prove it. But we don't whine about it, baby. It's part of the game. And so, I'm looking forward to this game. It's gonna be a fun game. Both teams are in position to do a lot of work in this division, as they say.

"The AFC North is on fire and I'm glad I'm in the kitchen because I like it that way. But those are words that were said and they will be addressed."

The Steelers put together a dominant performance against the Browns on Sunday, holding them to a season-low six points.

Verse struggled to make an impact in the contest, as the two-time Pro Bowler only finished with one tackle and one quarterback hit.
